chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not prescribe for women any making up (of missed fasts) nor any fasting except what He made obligatory upon them, which is the fasting of Ramadan; and He did not prescribe for them any prayer except what He made obligatory upon them, which is the prayer of the day and night, except that which is exempted from them due to menstruation and postpartum bleeding.
ai.seo_question: Do women need to make up missed prayers during menstruation?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this ruling to distinguish the nature of prayer as a time-bound act of worship (*ibadah muqayyadah*) from fasting, which is cumulative. This distinction underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that menstruation and postpartum bleeding constitute a state of ritual impurity (*hadath*) that suspends the obligation of prayer itself, rather than merely delaying it, thereby exempting women from *qada* (making up) the missed units.
